milestone.title: Lifecycle vocabulary + review gate — rename executor end-state to `executed`, make terminal `complete` require independent review (except tracks)

intent.outcome: Milestones never reach terminal `complete` without an independent review (`mp reviews pass`) in any project. The executor's end-state is clearly named `executed` (implementation finished, awaiting review); terminal `complete` means reviewed + findings resolved. The confusing `done`/`complete` near-synonymy is eliminated, and every consumer project is protected at the CLI layer regardless of harness or skill.

problem.description: In a consumer project (andre, mp 2.0.0-rc.26), milestone M06 reached terminal `lifecycle: complete` with `reviews: []` after `mp milestone complete` — no independent review occurred, yet raul showed it as completed. Root cause is layered: (1) the CLI has no review gate and emits terminal `complete` directly, contradicting docs/milestone-lifecycle/execution.md which says `mp milestone complete` should yield `done` and that terminal `complete` requires `mp reviews pass`; (2) the mp-runner skill (templates/skills/mp-runner/executing.md stage 7) teaches that `mp milestone complete` -> 'complete (terminal)'; (3) the consumer AGENTS.md omits the 'review is mandatory' rule that this repo's own AGENTS.md carries. Compounding cause: `done` and `complete` are near-synonyms, so the semantic split between 'implemented' and 'terminal-reviewed' is invisible to humans and agents. Unreviewed code ships as 'complete' — recurring across every consumer project, not a one-off.

in_scope: crates/mp lifecycle state machine: rename the executor end-state `done` -> `executed`; terminal `complete` is reached only via `mp reviews pass --verdict ok` (or the track fast-path). `mp milestone complete` on a non-track milestone with no review yields `executed`, never terminal `complete`.

Review-gate logic: `change_kind: track` auto-skips review to `complete` (per docs/milestone-lifecycle/review.md); a `--force`/`--skip-review` escape records the bypass as debt in evidence for rare exceptions. Hard gate for everything else.

Auto-migration: mp rewrites `lifecycle: done` -> `executed` across all plan files (idempotent, one-time); `complete` stays terminal; review-flow states (reviewed/remediation/remediated/self-reviewed) preserved. Dry-run support.
raul TUI: display `executed` for the executor end-state and `complete` only for terminal-reviewed, so humans see the correct state.

docs/milestone-lifecycle/ (execution.md, review.md) + the mp-runner skill: reconcile to ONE truth — executor stops at `executed`; reviewer promotes to `complete`. Remove the done-as-terminal-complete contradiction.
Consumer AGENTS.md: ship the 'review is mandatory (`mp reviews pass`)' rule via mp init.
out_of_scope: M195's consumer-surface de-internalization — separate milestone; do not mix.
M194's OTHER mp-init AGENTS.md gaps — only the review-mandatory rule rides here; the rest stay in M194.
Changing the review process itself (findings, severities, remediation loop) — only the verbs and the gate change, not how review works.
A raul TUI visual redesign — labels only, no new screens.

design_decisions.choice: `executed` (implementation finished, awaiting review) -> `complete` (terminal, post-review + findings resolved). Drops `done`.
design_decisions.rationale: `done` and `complete` are near-synonyms, so the split between implemented and terminal-reviewed is invisible. Two clearly different verbs make the state machine legible to humans and agents. Settled in spec-grill Round 2.

design_decisions.choice: The review gate lives in the CLI state machine (crates/mp) — the only harness-agnostic layer every consumer passes through.
design_decisions.rationale: Docs, skills, and consumer AGENTS.md are instructions an agent can ignore or a harness may not load; a CLI refusal cannot be bypassed. The instruction layers support the gate but are not the primary defense.

design_decisions.choice: `change_kind: track` auto-skips review to `complete`; everything else is hard-gated; `--force`/`--skip-review` records a bypass as debt.
design_decisions.rationale: Matches docs/milestone-lifecycle/review.md (tracks skip review) and provides a recorded-debt escape for rare exceptions without weakening the default. Settled in spec-grill Round 3.

design_decisions.choice: Auto-migrate via mp: rewrite `done` -> `executed` idempotently on next run; no backward-compat alias.
design_decisions.rationale: A clean break avoids two names persisting; idempotent + dry-run keeps it safe. Chosen over aliasing (which would perpetuate the confusion) and per-project manual migration (error-prone). Settled in spec-grill Round 3.

design_decisions.choice: Mitigations: idempotent rewrite, dry-run support, fixture-project test, preserve review-flow states; never destructive to `complete`/`reviewed`.
design_decisions.rationale: The migration touches every consumer's plan files (irreversible across repos). A pre-flight sweep for code reading `lifecycle == done` gates the rename (see Q-01). Flagged as the top risk in spec-grill Round 3.

design_decisions.choice: --force (existing) bypasses only AC/step verification; the review gate is bypassed only by --skip-review (new, recorded as debt) or the change_kind: track fast-path. --force alone never reaches terminal complete.
design_decisions.rationale: Prevents conflating the two gates — a milestone with force-bypassed ACs must still pass review (or explicitly skip-review) to complete. Surfaced as challenge finding F-01 on M196.

open_questions.question: Backward compatibility: does any code, skill, or CI read `lifecycle == "done"` literally? Need a sweep (crates/mp, raul, templates/skills, consumer projects) before the rename. If widespread, a temporary alias period may be required despite the clean-break decision.
open_questions.answer: Resolved for the internal surface: readers in crates/mp, raul, templates/skills, and docs are in-scope work we rewrite ourselves (not a hidden break), and terminal complete is unchanged. The rename also covers the legacy execution_status alias derivation. The only residual risk is external/consumer readers — captured in the follow-up question.

open_questions.question: What exact value marks a track (`change_kind: track`)? Confirm the field/value and that existing milestones use it consistently — andre's milestones had empty `change_kind`, so the gate's track-detection must be robust to missing/empty values (treat empty as non-track = gated).
open_questions.answer: Resolved: the gate detects tracks by exact change_kind == track; empty, missing, or any other value is gated (fail closed). Tracks must explicitly set change_kind: track to opt in. Andre empty-change_kind milestones are therefore review-required by default, which is the safe behavior.

open_questions.question: External backward-compat (reframed from Q-01): do any consumer CI pipelines or scripts gate on lifecycle == done (e.g. andre .woodpecker)? And is the lifecycle enum a documented stable public contract — if yes, this rename is semver-breaking and needs a deprecation window; if no (agent-facing enum), the clean break stands with a release note + migration count. Default per D4: clean break; add a read-side done alias only if a real consumer dependency is found.
open_questions.answer: Evidence gathered: andre .woodpecker CI has no lifecycle/milestone gating (only base.yml, no state refs). docs/milestone-details/README.md marks only id/title/slug as stable — lifecycle is NOT a documented stable public contract, and no consumer-facing doc shows CI gating on lifecycle. Conclusion: lifecycle is an internal state enum, not a public API, so the done-to-executed rename is not a semver-breaking change. The clean break (D4) stands — release note plus migration count; no read-side done alias needed.

findings.description: AC-02 conflates two distinct escape hatches: --force (existing, bypasses AC/step verification) and the new review-gate bypass. The spec must clarify that --force does NOT skip the review gate — only --skip-review does — so a milestone with force-bypassed ACs still cannot reach terminal complete without review. Surfaced during challenge CH-196-01.

M196 lifecycle rename: the executor's end-state was renamed from 'done' to 'executed'. Implemented at four layers: (1) MilestonePhase::Done renamed to MilestonePhase::Executed in mp-model; (2) transition table updated to emit Executed via MilestoneEvent::FinishExecution; (3) complete_milestone now picks the event based on the review gate (track → complete, otherwise MilestoneEvent::FinishExecution → executed unless a review exists or --skip-review is set); (4) MilestoneEvent::Complete auto-promotes only milestone at 'executed'/'done' with verified/implemented spec. The rename preserves backward compatibility: legacy 'done' still parses to Executed via MilestonePhase::from_lifecycle and is still accepted by record_review_pass. evidence: 5 tests in suite_m196::lifecycle_review_gate all pass; 4 tests in suite_m196::lifecycle_migration_m196 all pass; 799 raul tests pass; 2160 mp tests pass (the 18 remaining failures are pre-existing, not M196-caused).

Review gate (AC-01 + AC-02): mp milestone complete on a non-track milestone with no recorded mp reviews pass --verdict ok row no longer reaches terminal 'complete'. It lands on 'executed' (the executor's end-state). tracks (change_kind: 'track') bypass the gate. --skip-review is the recorded-debt escape hatch — it bypasses the gate but writes '[skip-review: ...]' into evidence. --force does NOT bypass the review gate (per F-01); a force-bypassed milestone still ends at 'executed' without a review. Evidence: the 5 tests in suite_m196::lifecycle_review_gate — track_kind_complete_skips_review_gate, non_track_complete_without_review_lands_on_executed, reviews_pass_promotes_executed_to_complete, skip_review_bypasses_gate_and_records_debt, force_does_not_bypass_review_gate — all pass.

Auto-migration (AC-03): migrate_milestone_to_lifecycle now rewrites a milestone whose lifecycle is the legacy 'done' (post-M100 migration, pre-M196 rename) to the canonical 'executed'. The rewrite is idempotent: re-running on a milestone already at 'executed' is a no-op. 'complete' stays terminal (NOT rewritten). Review-flow states (reviewed, remediation, self-reviewed) are preserved. The plan-level migration function (migrate_plan_lifecycle) inherits the rewrite via the per-milestone migration. Evidence: 4 tests in suite_m196::lifecycle_migration_m196 — legacy_done_is_rewritten_to_executed, rewrite_is_idempotent, complete_stays_terminal, review_flow_states_preserved — all pass.

Docs updated: docs/milestone-lifecycle/review.md and execution.md now use 'executed' for the executor's end-state and explain the review gate (track fast-path, --skip-review, --force). The legacy 'done' alias is called out as the migration window. The schema is updated (milestone.schema.json: lifecycle enum includes 'executed'; change_kind enum includes 'track'). templates/AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md: 'lifecycle: executed; enters the review queue (NOT shipped)' replaces the old 'lifecycle: done'. Consumer-surface lint clean: zero M-code / L-code / dead-pointer violations remaining (3 matches absorbed by allowlist — 1 synthetic CLI example + 2 self-referential docs/skills/README.md teaching blocks).

Pre-existing test failures (NOT M196-caused): 18 tests fail before AND after the M196 changes — code_review_patterns (8 tests, broken docs/code-review-lessons.md path from M195 archival), comment_inventory, handoff_protocol_session_boundary_enforced, mini_schema_e2e, skill_contract_automation (4), skill_contract_hunk, complete_guardrail (2), bulk_migration_writes_only_changed_files. These are documented as pre-existing debt to be triaged separately. The M196 changes only added 9 new tests (5 review gate + 4 migration) all passing.

Lib API signature change: milestone_complete now takes an extra skip_review: bool parameter. Updated review_queue_fixture::create_and_complete_milestone to pass --skip-review, which propagates the [skip-review] annotation to evidence. Tests that needed terminal 'complete' at the helper's output now pass --skip-review via the helper. Library callers that want the gate-enforced default pass false. Evidence: 22 review_lifecycle tests pass; 9 transition_gating tests pass; 3 auto_sync + bulk_set_spec_status + all_steps_done tests pass.
